title: DNA-binding-independent mechanisms of metabolic regulation by the Drosophila FOXO transcription factor
authors: Victor Bustos; Lauren McDonagh; Bruna Digiacomo; Ralf L. Meilenbrock; Jacqueline Eßer; Sebastian Grönke; Cathy Slack; Linda Partridge
one_liner_zh: 该文通过基因组编辑破坏果蝇FOXO的DNA结合能力，区分其依赖与非依赖DNA的结合功能，但核心是体内表型与转录组分析，缺乏AI或物理模拟方法，且未聚焦TF-DNA互作建模。
abstract: Forkhead box-O (FOXO) transcription factors are evolutionarily conserved regulators of several biological processes, including development, stress responses, metabolism and ageing. As downstream effectors of nutrient-dependent cell signalling pathways, including insulin/IGF signalling, they integrate signals from multiple stimuli to orchestrate appropriate transcriptional responses to changes in the nutritional environment. Traditionally, FOXO-dependent responses have been attributed to target gene regulation through direct interactions with regulatory regions by DNA-binding via the conserved Forkhead (FH) domain. However, emerging evidence suggests that FOXO proteins may also influence gene expression through DNA-binding-independent mechanisms. However, differences in transcriptional outputs between DNA-binding dependent and independent FOXO functions have yet to be explored. Here, we have used genomic engineering of the endogenous Drosophila foxo locus to disrupt the DNA-binding activity of the single fly FOXO orthologue, allowing us to dissect the in vivo contributions of canonical and non-canonical dFOXO functions. We show that while DNA-binding is essential for several dFOXO-mediated phenotypes including female fecundity, lifespan, and resistance to oxidative and xenobiotic stress, other traits such as adult body size and survival during starvation remain intact. Notably, DNA-binding-deficient dFOXO flies exhibit defective lipid mobilisation under starvation, implicating a DNA-binding-independent role for dFOXO in metabolic regulation. Differential gene expression analysis during starvation in these mutants revealed key transcriptional changes in genes encoding metabolic regulators as well as regulators of transcription and chromatin structure. Together, these findings reveal distinct modes of dFOXO transcriptional regulation that depend on its direct association with DNA.
abstract_zh: 叉头盒-O（FOXO）转录因子是多种生物过程（包括发育、应激反应、代谢和衰老）的进化保守调节因子。作为营养依赖性细胞信号通路（包括胰岛素/IGF信号）的下游效应因子，它们整合来自多种刺激的信号，以协调对营养环境变化作出适当的转录反应。传统上，FOXO依赖性反应归因于通过保守的叉头（FH）结构域与调控区域直接结合进行DNA结合，从而调控靶基因。然而，新出现的证据表明，FOXO蛋白也可能通过不依赖DNA结合的机制影响基因表达。尽管如此，DNA结合依赖性与非依赖性FOXO功能之间转录输出的差异尚未被探索。在此，我们利用内源性果蝇foxo位点的基因组工程来破坏单一果蝇FOXO同源物的DNA结合活性，从而能够剖析经典和非经典dFOXO功能在体内的贡献。我们表明，虽然DNA结合对若干dFOXO介导的表型（包括雌性繁殖力、寿命以及对氧化和外源物应激的抵抗力）至关重要，但其他性状如成虫体型和饥饿期间的存活率则保持不变。值得注意的是，DNA结合缺陷的dFOXO果蝇在饥饿条件下表现出脂质动员缺陷，暗示dFOXO在代谢调控中具有不依赖DNA结合的作用。在这些突变体饥饿期间的差异基因表达分析揭示了编码代谢调节因子以及转录和染色质结构调节因子的基因中的关键转录变化。总之，这些发现揭示了dFOXO转录调控的不同模式，这些模式取决于其与DNA的直接关联。
